original_query: select sum(l_extendedprice) / 7.0 as avg_yearly from lineitem, part where p_partkey = l_partkey and p_brand = 'Brand#32' and p_container = 'WRAP PKG' and l_quantity < ( select 0.2 * avg(l_quantity) from lineitem where l_partkey = p_partkey );
rewritten_query:
SELECT SUM(l_extendedprice) / 7.0 AS avg_yearly
FROM (
    SELECT l.l_extendedprice,
           l.l_quantity,
           0.2 * AVG(l.l_quantity) OVER (PARTITION BY l.l_partkey) AS avg_quantity_threshold
    FROM lineitem l
    JOIN part p ON p.p_partkey = l.l_partkey
    WHERE p.p_brand = 'Brand#32'
      AND p.p_container = 'WRAP PKG'
) AS li
WHERE li.l_quantity < li.avg_quantity_threshold;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Replace the correlated scalar subquery (0.2 * AVG(l_quantity) per p_partkey) with a window function AVG(l_quantity) OVER (PARTITION BY l_partkey), computed once after filtering to matching parts instead of re-scanning lineitem per row.

Push the selective part predicates (p_brand = 'Brand#32' AND p_container = 'WRAP PKG') into the inner subquery/join so the average is computed only for the ~0.1% matching part keys, reducing the window input from millions of rows to roughly tens of thousands.

Convert the comma join with join filter into an explicit inner JOIN between lineitem and part before the window computation, allowing a hash join with the small filtered part set to prune lineitem early.

Compute the threshold (0.2 * AVG) in the inner query and apply the quantity comparison in the outer query, ensuring the average is taken over all lineitem rows of each matching part (not only qualifying rows), preserving exact equivalence.
